generators typically use the following
mechanisms:
Option D) Associativity and Precedence: This is
the most common method to resolve shift-
reduce conflicts. Operators in programming | |
languages often have associativity (whether
operations are evaluated left-to-right or right-to-
left) and precedence (which operation takes
precedence over another). By specifying the
associativity and precedence of operators in the
grammar, the parser can decide whether to shift
or reduce based on the current operator and the
one at the top of the stack.
Associativity: Determines the direction (left or
right) in which operations of the same
precedence are evaluated. For example, in many
programming languages, addition and
subtraction are left-associative.
Precedence: Determines the order of operations
when multiple operators are present. For
example, multiplication has higher precedence
than addition.
Option A) Left Recursion: Left recursion is a
parsing technique where the left-most non-
terminal symbol in a production rule appears
again as the first symbol in the right-hand side of
the rule. Left recursion can sometimes lead to
conflicts, but it is not typically used to resolve
shift-reduce conflicts directly.
Option B) Left Factoring: Left factoring is a
technique used to refactor grammar rules to
eliminate common prefixes. This technique can
help in reducing the number of conflicts but is
not directly used to resolve shift-reduce conflicts.
Option C) Ambiguity: Ambiguity in grammar can
lead to conflicts, including shift-reduce conflicts.
Resolving ambiguity involves restructuring the
grammar to remove multiple interpretations of
the same input string, but this does not directly
resolve shift-reduce conflicts.
So option D is the correct answer.

content.value: The techniques used to handle the phantom problem are A. Time stamping B. Index locking C. Predicate locking D. Execution indexing Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Option A) The basic timestamp ordering protocol
(BASIC T/O) allows reads and writes on database
objects without using locks. Instead, every
database object X is tagged with a timestamp of
the last transaction that successfully performed a
read (denoted as R-TS(X)) or write (denoted as
W-TS(X)) on that object. The DBMS then checks
these timestamps for every operation. If a
transaction tries to access an object in a way that
violates the timestamp order, the transaction is
aborted and restarted
For dynamic databases in which transactions
perform insertions, updates, and deletions time
stamping will not be sufficient.
The phantom phenomenon arises when two
transactions logically conflict even though they
do not lock a common data item. In a database,
the phantom problem is a scenario where a
transaction reads a set of rows from the
database that match a certain condition, and
when the same transaction attempts to read the
rows again (using the same condition), it
discovers additional rows that weren't there
previously. These new rows are known as
'phantoms'.
Approaches to Address the Phantom Problem:
1. Re-Execute Scans: Transactions may re-run
queries at commit time to check for different
results, indicating missed changes due to new or
deleted records.
2. Predicate Locking: This involves acquiring locks
based on the predicates of the queries, ensuring
that any data that satisfies the predicate cannot
be modified by other transactions.A predicate
lock in database systems is a type of lock that
prevents the modification of all data rows that
satisfy a specific condition, thus ensuring data
integrity when multiple transactions access the
same data simultaneously.
3. Index Locking: Utilizing index keys to protect
ranges of data, preventing phantoms by ensuring
that no new data can fall within the locked
ranges. After an index range is locked, no other
transaction can insert, update, or delete any row
within this range until the transaction that holds
the lock completes. In this way, index locking
ensures the consistent state of a transaction,
resolving the phantom problem.
Option D) Indexing often refers to the process of
creating and maintaining data that allow for
efficient access to elements based on some key
or index. For dynamic database concurrency
problems like phantom problem indexing is not
alone sufficient.

content.value: Techniques for performing I/O : A. Programmed I/O B. Interrupt-driven I/O C. Rotational I/O D. Direct memory access E. Channelized I/O Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

explanation.value:
A. Programmed I/O:
In programmed I/O, the CPU controls data
transfer between external devices and memory
directly using I/O instructions. This method
involves the CPU actively waiting for each I/O
operation to complete before proceeding, which
can be inefficient for large data transfers.
B. Interrupt-driven I/O:
Interrupt-driven I/O allows the CPU to handle
other tasks while waiting for I/O operations to
complete. When an I/O operation finishes, the
device sends an interrupt signal to the CPU,
prompting it to handle the completed operation.
This approach reduces CPU idle time and
improves overall system efficiency.
D. Direct Memory Access (DMA):
DMA allows external devices to transfer data
directly to or from memory without CPU
intervention. A DMA controller manages the data
transfer, freeing the CPU to perform other
tasks.This method significantly reduces CPU
overhead and speeds up data transfer rates
between devices and memory.
C. Rotational I/O:
Rotational I/O is not a standard term for
describing I/O techniques in general computing
contexts. It refers to specific operations in disk
drives where data is read or written as the disk
rotates, but it's not commonly listed as a general
I/O technique.
E. Channelized I/O:
Channelized I/O involves using specialized
hardware channels or controllers to manage I/O
operations independently of the CPU. It's
commonly used in mainframe and high-
performance computing environments to offload
I/O processing from the CPU, but it's less
commonly categorized as a fundamental I/O
technique compared to programmed I/O,
interrupt-driven I/O, and DMA.
So option B is the correct answer.
